title: Isaac, 26: Leaving $1,500 a Year on the Table

scenes.say: Isaac turned down $1,500 a year in free money from his employer.
His job matches 50 cents per dollar he saves, up to 6% of his $50,000 salary.
He skipped the retirement plan, thinking he couldn't afford it.
But it comes out before tax. $3,000 a year cost him roughly $100 per paycheck.
That's an instant 50% boost before any investing even happens.
Just the match, if it grew roughly 7% a year, not guaranteed, could reach about $150,000 in 30 years.

items.text: Save at least up to the match

scenes.say: Does your job match? Subscribe so you don't make this mistake on your next paycheck, because that's $1,500 free, and he said no.

visual.text: Does your job have a match?

question: Does your employer offer a match, and are you getting all of it?
description: Isaac's employer matches 50% of what he saves, up to 6% of his $50,000 salary, which is about $1,500 a year he was skipping. Saving $3,000 pre-tax cost him roughly $100 per paycheck. If the match alone grew about 7% a year (not guaranteed), it could reach around $150,000 in 30 years. Rounded estimates for general education.
